item.title: Brazil's tight runoff tests Trump officials' bid to bring Bolsonaros back to power
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
By Gabriel Stargardter SAO PAULO, Oct 24 (Reuters) - Two US State Department officials led a campaign to restore the right-wing Bolsonaro clan to power in Brazil and successfully pushed for sanctions aimed at tilting the election in their favor, according to 10 current and former US officials with direct knowledge of the matter. Their plan faces a reckoning on Sunday, when Senator Flavio Bolsonaro faces leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in a tight run-off. Lula has warned Washington against encroaching on Brazil's sovereignty and accused his opponent of plotting with the Trump administration. The two officials were Darren Beattie, a Senior Advisor ‌for Western Hemisphere Affairs who oversees Brazil policy, and Ricardo Pita, another senior advisor promoted this year to Deputy Assistant Secretary for North America. The details of their campaign to return the Bolsonaros to power haven't been previously reported. Beattie and Pita, both political appointees, operated with wide latitude to manage Washington's relationship with the ‌second most-populous country in the Americas, the people said. In the months before election campaigning began, they instructed US diplomats in Brazil that it was US policy to restore former President Jair Bolsonaro as Brazil’s leader – even though he had been disqualified from office for plotting a coup in 2022, when he lost the presidential election to Lula, three of the people said. After Bolsonaro received a 27-year sentence in September 2025, the two men pivoted to ​supporting the candidacy of his son, right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the three sources said. Beattie and Pita told embassy staff not to interact with other conservative presidential contenders who could challenge the younger Bolsonaro, they said. Since last year, the two men have successfully advocated for punitive US government measures on Brazil designed to weaken Lula and boost the Bolsonaros, the 10 people told Reuters. The policies included designating Brazilian gangs as terrorist groups and imposing US sanctions against the Brazilian Supreme Court Justice who was spearheading the investigation into Jair Bolsonaro. Reuters could not determine the extent to which the two men were acting on orders from the White House or Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Trump, a vocal defender of Bolsonaro since his election defeat in 2022, hasn’t publicly endorsed any candidate. The White House declined to comment and referred questions to the State Department. State Department Spokesman Tommy Pigott didn't answer questions about specific measures and directives involving Beattie and Pita but said in a statement: "All actions taken by the United States against narco-traffickers and to protect free speech are to defend the rights and lives of the American people. The Brazilian people have the right to ‌choose their leaders through free and fair elections." Lula’s office did not respond to comment requests. Orna Blum, one of the officials who ⁠spoke to Reuters about Beattie and Pita’s efforts, led the State Department's Brazil and Southern Cone office until retiring last year over her opposition to the Trump administration. Washington "has every right to pursue its economic and strategic interests," she said. "But when American foreign policy instruments are used to pressure another democracy over the legal fate of a political ally, the line between diplomacy and political intervention has been crossed." SANCTIONS ON A SUPREME COURT JUSTICE Beattie is a former White House speechwriter fired in 2018 after addressing an event frequented by white nationalists. He’s also the architect of "free speech ⁠diplomacy," a policy advocated by Trump allies that seeks to punish nations they accuse of censoring right-wing speech by US citizens, companies and global right-wing allies. The United States has accused Brazil Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes of violating free speech rights by jailing Brazilians for political social-media posts and by censoring content of US social-media companies. Moraes has argued he was ridding social media of fake news that undermined public faith in Brazil's democratic institutions. Moraes did not respond to a comment request. Pita, a conservative Venezuelan-American, is among many in Rubio's orbit who view Lula as a threat to US interests in Latin America. Rubio has been a key leader in the administration’s aggressive policy in the region, which has included an invasion of Venezuela to oust its president, an oil blockade of Cuba, and military attacks ​on suspected ​drug boats from Latin America. Beattie and Pita were drawn to the Bolsonaro family’s right-wing politics, their antipathy towards Lula, and the idea that Jair Bolsonaro was a victim of abuses by Brazil's Supreme Court. Like ​Trump in the 2020 US election, Bolsonaro refused to concede he lost Brazil’s 2022 presidential vote, triggering riots by supporters who stormed government ‌buildings. The Supreme Court convicted him in September 2025 of plotting a coup to remain in power. Before the conviction, in early 2025, the Bolsonaros were aggressively lobbying Washington for sanctions under the Global Magnitsky Human Rights Accountability Act against Moraes, who had led criminal investigations into Jair Bolsonaro. The act is a 2016 federal law allowing US sanctions against foreign individuals responsible for human-rights abuses or severe corruption. Around April 2025, Jair Bolsonaro’s younger son, Eduardo, visited Beattie in his State Department office in Washington DC, according to two former US officials. Eduardo Bolsonaro had been making the public case for Magnitsky sanctions against Moraes since at least 2024, and in March 2025 he said in a livestream that it was "practically certain" the Trump administration would do so. Eduardo Bolsonaro did not respond to requests for comment. Beattie made calls to the US Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control to appeal for Magnitsky sanctions against Moraes, said a former US official with direct knowledge of the matter. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, whose department administers Magnitsky sanctions through OFAC, offered no opposition, the former official said. The US announced Magnitsky sanctions against Moraes in July 2025, citing his alleged violations of free-speech rights by censoring anti-government social-media posts. A Treasury official said Bessent and Rubio are "fully aligned on the administration’s foreign policy." TERRORIST DESIGNATIONS The Bolsonaro family was also pushing for Washington to designate Brazil's top gangs – the Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) and Comando Vermelho (CV) – as terrorist organizations. They believed such a designation would hurt Lula, ‌who some opponents have criticized for failing to control crime. Eduardo Bolsonaro had become friends with Pita through US conservative circles, and both supported the effort to designate the gangs as terrorist groups. In May 2025, ​Pita joined a US delegation that visited Jair Bolsonaro at his residence in Brasilia as he awaited his trial, according to public announcements at the time. Also in the group: David Gamble, the State Department’s top sanctions ​official at the time. Back in Washington, Pita asked State sanctions officials to explore how terrorist designations like those announced against Mexican cartels in February 2025 could be used ​in Brazil, one former official said. Nearly a year later, in May 2026 – after Pita was promoted to a new job that pulled him out of Brazil affairs – presidential contender Flavio Bolsonaro met with Beattie and Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau in Washington to discuss "the urgency of designating the ‌PCC and the Comando Vermelho as foreign terrorist organizations," according to an X post by right-wing influencer Paulo Figueiredo that included ​photos of the attendees. The State Department announced the designation the following day. Reuters could not determine the ​extent of Pita or Beattie’s influence in securing the final decision. BACKFIRES AND SETBACKS In July 2025, Washington also announced a series of other measures against Brazil, including the revocations of eight Supreme Court justices' visas and 50% tariffs on Brazilian goods, citing the "persecution" of Jair Bolsonaro. Reuters could not determine what, if any, role Beattie or Pita played in the additional measures. But if they were intended to undermine Lula, many of them backfired, according to political analysts in Brazil. Measures targeting the court did nothing to stop it from proceeding with Bolsonaro's trial, while the tariffs boosted the Lula government's poll numbers, the analysts said. Major US and Brazilian firms reliant on bilateral trade – including ​meatpacking giant JBS - controlled by Brazilian billionaires Wesley and Joesley Batista – also pushed back on the tariffs, which Washington eventually watered down. Beattie ‌and Pita’s campaign also hit setbacks. Without an official explanation from the Treasury Department, the US removed Justice Moraes from the Magnitsky sanctions list in December, and in March Brazil barred Beattie from entering the country to visit Bolsonaro in prison. Mario Braga, a Latin America analyst at risk intelligence firm RANE, ​said Trump may have decided to withhold a public endorsement of Bolsonaro to avoid being seen as meddling in Brazil's election – a perception that could boost Lula’s popularity. Still, after Flavio Bolsonaro narrowly outperformed Lula in the first-round election earlier this month, Trump called it a big victory. "Close, but a very, very ​big victory," he told reporters. "Amazing, actually." (Reporting by Gabriel StargardterAdditional reporting by Gram Slattery in Washington, Luciana Magalhaes in Sao Paulo, Lisandra Paraguassu in Brasilia Editing by Brad Haynes and Richard Valdmanis) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/inside-trump-administration-campaign-return-214506018.html

item.title: 'Weaponizing the law': California AG slams DOJ's attack on alleged noncitizen voting
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
People cast their ballots at St Mary's Episcopal church during the first day of early voting in Los Angeles, California, on Saturday. Photograph: Chris Torres/EPA California’s attorney general on Saturday rebuked the Trump administration’s efforts to quash alleged noncitizen voting, calling it “politicizing and weaponizing the law”. Rob Bonta, the state’s attorney general, said the justice department acted at Donald Trump’s direction. “It is once again the United States Department of Justice politicizing and weaponizing the law to attack its enemies, and it is completely improper,” he told MS Now. Less than two weeks before the midterms, federal prosecutors called upon California election officials to verify within 48 hours a list of about 20,000 ballots belonging to suspected noncitizens. Noncitizen voting is extremely rare , but in the run-up to the midterm elections, the justice department has ramped up prosecutions of people accused of illegally voting while not holding US citizenship. California’s election personnel have raised concern that the administration’s directive could disenfranchise citizens. Los Angeles officials said this week a “high percentage” of the individuals on the list were born in the United States. “Trump’s DOJ is so desperate to invent ‘widespread voter fraud,’ it sent California counties lists of people who NEVER voted – and voters from the WRONG COUNTY. Absolute clown show!” California’s governor Gavin Newsom posted on social media . “Voter intimidation has no place in our democracy,” Pete Aguilar, a congressman representing south-west San Bernardino county, said in a social media post . The federal government’s oversight attempts come amid a national Republican effort to crack down on alleged voter fraud, particularly any cases among undocumented immigrants. “We are asking each county election official to commit to working with us by providing the necessary information for DHS to quickly verify citizenship status. With their help, we can ensure the most secure election in California history,” the justice department said. Bonta, the California attorney general, has raised questions about the evidence behind the suspected noncitizen ballots. “All they provided was a list of people and nothing about why they’re purportedly ineligible. If they have such information, we would be happy to review it, but they’ve provided none,” Bonta said at a recent press conference. The DoJ also charged 28 foreign nationals recently, accusing them of fraudulently registering to vote. “Today’s arrests prove what we have been saying,” Bill Essayli, first assistant US attorney, said in a statement. “California is mailing ballots to noncitizens, and they are refusing to comply with federal law, which makes it a crime for noncitizens to vote. The voting rights of American citizens must be protected.” The defendants are lawful permanent residents, who have legal status in the US but are not citizens authorized to vote. Some state officials took no action on Friday’s letters, citing the fast-approaching election, which spurred a legal battle with the justice department. An appeals court is set to hear the matter on Tuesday. This article originally appeared on The Guardian at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/california-leaders-rebuke-trump-administration-001617824.html

item.title: Musk says he was behind Starlink disruptions, claiming Ukraine service violations
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Elon Musk said on Saturday that his company SpaceX had throttled the Starlink satellite internet service in Ukraine, disrupting operations that the country relies on to defend itself against Russia. Musk's admission on social media came after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that Ukraine’s access to Starlink and Starshield satellite links has been restored to the speeds it had before restrictions that disrupted front-line operations for more than a week. Questions have persisted since last week about who ordered the interruptions to the Musk-made satellite internet system that Kyiv has relied on for years to counter Moscow’s attacks . “The speeds are now where they need to be,” Zelenskyy wrote on X, adding that restoration began overnight and were sufficient by Saturday morning, improving front-line logistics and defense against Russian jet-powered Shahed drones. Musk admits he was behind Starlink’s speed restriction After Ukraine said the services had been restored, Elon Musk spoke out on the speed restrictions that began last week. In a post Saturday on X, Musk acknowledged that his company SpaceX throttled the Starlink satellite internet service. “Using Starlink, a civilian commercial service, for offensive drone strikes to kill people has never been allowed, nor should it be,” Musk wrote. “Ukraine military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people. That loophole was closed last week.” But he maintained that the U.S. government controlled whatever changes happened with Starshield, the military-grade version of Starlink that is the backbone of Ukraine’s drone operations and communication. He also defended the role of SpaceX in bolstering Ukraine’s defenses since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Restrictions imposed last week on Starshield alarmed the country’s military and government officials, with commanders reporting lost drones and disrupted missions. The restoration follows a new U.S. diplomatic push to end the war. Russia agreed Wednesday to resume three-way negotiations with Washington and Kyiv next month. On Friday, Kyiv and Moscow also agreed to a localized ceasefire brokered by first lady Melania Trump around Oleshky , a war-ravaged, Russian-occupied town in Ukraine’s southern Kherson region. Restriction led to tensions between Ukraine and the US The episode added to tensions between Kyiv and Washington, a relationship already strained by President Donald Trump’s reported deal with Moscow on Russian diesel imports, which Ukraine viewed as a betrayal. Ukraine's Defense Minister Yevhenii Khmara credited “direct dialogue” and Zelenskyy’s diplomacy with Washington, adding that the outcome mattered most “for our front, for the military, the work of drones, logistics and communications.” Trump has maintained that he didn’t make the call, while also saying Musk should not be blamed. Vice President JD Vance has hinted at White House coordination with Musk, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth have denied any administration involvement. Russia and Ukraine have continued to target each other Meanwhile, a man was killed and two others wounded in a missile attack on the city of Lozova in Ukraine's Kharkiv region, local officials said Saturday. Moscow-installed authorities in cities across Russia-occupied Crimea reported power blackouts Saturday following overnight Ukrainian attacks. Ukraine’s General Staff said Saturday that its forces hit a chemical plant in the Russian city of Tolyatti, which produces materials used in rocket fuel. Tolyatti Mayor Ilya Sukhikh said the overnight attack damaged industrial facilities in the city. Ukrainian forces also hit an electronics plant in the city of Oryol, Ukraine’s General Staff confirmed Saturday. Local officials in Oryol said Saturday that three people were killed in Friday’s attack. The General Staff said the plant makes components for the cruise and ballistic missiles Russia fires at Ukrainian cities. Ukrainian drones also reached Russia’s Omsk region in western Siberia, more than 2,000 kilometers (1,242 miles) from the border with Ukraine. Omsk regional Gov. Vitaly Khotsenko said drones “reached a northern industrial hub.” Online retailer Ozon said Saturday that its logistics center in Omsk has been attacked by a drone, but there were no casualties. Ozon is a competitor to Wildberries, whose facilities Ukraine has also targeted. ___ Morton reported from London. ___ Follow the AP’s coverage of the war in Ukraine at https://apnews.com/hub/russia-ukraine This article originally appeared on Associated Press at https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/ukraine-says-starlink-speed-limits-104548676.html

item.title: Obama rebukes Ramaswamy over Acton ad and hits Trump on costs at Ohio rally
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
In his first rally of the 2026 midterm cycle, former President Barack Obama slammed President Donald Trump and Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy, calling out the latter’s much-maligned campaign ad centering on Democrat Amy Acton’s mother. “There's gotta be something inside you where you just say no office is worth stooping that low,” Obama said of Ramaswamy’s choice to run the ad. With the midterms just over a week away, Obama was rallying in Cleveland in support of Acton and Democratic Senate candidate Sherrod Brown. Trump, Obama said, had broken a slew of promises he made on the campaign trail in 2024, ensnaring the country in an ongoing war in Iran and failing to bring down costs. Instead, “he’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory,” the former president said, taking aim at Trump’s renovations to the executive mansion. “We got two more years of this administration,” he said. “That’s how our system of government works. But you know what we’re not stuck with? We’re not stuck with a spineless Congress and Republican governors who are enabling lawlessness and carelessness and cruelty and indifference for working people.” Long one of Democrats' top surrogates , Obama is again stepping off the sidelines in the closing stretch of an election. He’ll appear in Detroit alongside Democrats Abdul El-Sayed and Jocelyn Benson on Sunday, after which he’ll travel to Georgia for a rally with Sen. Jon Ossoff and former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms on Oct. 28. The former president, who captured Ohio’s electoral votes in 2008 and 2012, also called out Ramaswamy for his controversial campaign ad featuring Acton’s mother . Acton was removed from her mother’s home after her stepfather was charged with raping her. She spoke about her childhood in a speech moments before the former president took to the stage on Saturday. “There's a decency that we should expect out of our public officials,” Obama said. “And I don't know what's happened where the standards of behavior have gotten so low that somebody could run an ad like that.” The White House and Ramaswamy’s campaign both did not immediately respond to requests for comment. This article originally appeared on Politico at https://www.politico.com/news/2026/10/24/obama-slams-ramaswamy-trump-ohio-rally-midterms-01134765

item.title: Met Police received claims about Meghan's father, but didn't share with other agencies
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, said she is "deeply distressed" by the news that her father, Thomas Markle, is under investigation over claims he possessed images containing child sexual abuse in his home. The images were reportedly found in his home in the Philippines after he returned to the U.S. in May, Philippine officials said. Thomas Markle denied the allegations, calling them "sick lies" and "the worst thing anyone could accuse me of." London’s Metropolitan Police confirmed Saturday that it received a letter in January 2019 containing “a number of claims about alleged offending outside the United Kingdom,” the BBC reported . The letter was sent to the force’s protection command because of concerns about the duchess’s security. The Met said it passed the letter to the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex “for their awareness,” but did not share the details with other law enforcement agencies. The force said it is reviewing how it handled the matter and considering whether to refer itself to the Independent Office for Police Conduct, the police watchdog. In a statement through her spokesperson, Meghan Markle said that she is "deeply distressed" by the news, and that she was first made aware of the claims by the Met Police in 2018. "I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed," Meghan's statement said. "In 2018, a letter was sent to the Metropolitan police and Royalty and Specialist Protection. That letter was subsequently shared with me. It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father, and I was given assurances that these were being investigated. "I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications' distortion over the years, any distance from my father, and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them. "I trusted that the authorities were doing the same for other families. "Although the breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine, my sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children." Meghan had said the letter was sent in 2018. A spokesman for the duchess said Saturday that “any discrepancy of a few months” was “an understandable consequence of that passage of time.” Authorities in the Philippines are also investigating. Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said national police had secured Markle’s computer for a forensic examination, the BBC reported. The allegations, reported by Mail Online , said Thomas Markle is under investigation after being reported by his son, Thomas Markle Jr. In a statement to Mail Online , the elder Markle said: "I'm shocked, I'm hurt and I'm very upset that my son is making these accusations against me. I could never do what I'm being accused of. It's the worst thing anyone could accuse me of.” He added: "It's just a bunch of lies. It's sick. I have no idea why Tom [Markle] is trying to destroy me with these lies." Yahoo has contacted the Met Office and authorities in the U.S. and the Philippines for comment. This article originally appeared on Yahoo News at https://www.yahoo.com/news/world/article/met-police-says-it-received-2019-letter-with-claims-about-meghans-father-but-didnt-share-it-with-other-agencies-163535130.html
